data.narrative:
Aurora Innovation, a public-stage autonomous systems company founded by Urmson, Anderson, and Bagnell, has raised approximately $2.5B to date. The drones and autonomous sector contains a limited peer universe of 7 private companies, with no public comparables available for direct valuation triangulation.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The sector contains only five companies meeting narrow definitional filters (Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, Elroy Air), which falls short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. Same-stage peers number only two; no adjacent-stage or similar-tier comparables exist within the drones and autonomous segment. An all-sector median approach would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of business models and development timelines across broader autonomous technology categories.

Without sufficient peer density to support comparable-company analysis, traditional equity valuation methods prove structurally constrained. The absence of public trading comparables further limits market-based anchoring. A defensible valuation range cannot be derived from the available data. Analysis would require either expansion to qualitatively adjacent sectors (with explicit methodology disclosure of cross-sector assumptions), application of venture-backed cost-of-capital methods, or revenue multiples if underlying financial metrics were provided. Key uncertainties include Aurora's current revenue base, path to profitability, and technical validation milestones—none of which are present in the current dataset.
